_comment: Role-based unit stats for the Rommel's Arrival OOB, derived from the CNA Unit Characteristics Charts (German [4.46c], Commonwealth [4.46a]) in the VASSAL mod -- see memory cna-unit-stats-source. Each role notes the chart type code it is taken from. IMPORTANT: this is a CLOSE-ASSAULT-ONLY approximation for the current engine. CPA and Close Assault Off/Def come straight from the charts for infantry/recon; but barrage (artillery), anti-armor (AT), the tank-model close-assault system (rule 15.4), morale, and reinforcement arrival are DEFERRED engine mechanics -- so artillery/AT are given oca 0 (no close-assault punch, they defend only) and tanks a representative close-assault value from their historical models. steps = starting TOE strength (charted Maximum TOE, i.e. full strength).
_aa_air_comment: Two roles added in Phase 3.1 so the Order of Battle stops losing whole categories. 'aa' is the Anti-Aircraft-Type combat unit (rule 3.23); it is a Pure Flak unit (rule 46.17: only AA points -> is_pure_aa, free stacking in Major Cities per 9.16b), and its ground stats here are a FLAGGED PROXY (charted CPA 15, motorized, weak (1)/(1) close assault proxied oca 0/dca 1) pending the per-model Light/Heavy AA rows of [4.47]/[4.48]/[4.49] in Phase 3.2, which override anti_armor for the heavy flak (the 88 / 90-53). 'sgsu' is the Squadron Ground Support Unit (rules 3.21 / 35.0), and in Phase 5.1 it REPLACED the inert 'air' carrier role: the Air Landing Strips and flying-boat Alighting areas that shared that role are no longer units at all but game.state.AirFacility installations (rule 36), so only the SGSU counters are still units. Its stats are the rulebook's where the rulebook states them -- 35.12 'they are vehicles', 'they have no Stacking Point Value' (sp 0), 'no combat strength of any type' (oca/dca 0, is_combat false) -- with ONE FLAGGED PROXY, AND SAY EXACTLY WHICH CELL IT IS: 35.12 says the Capability Point Allowance is 'printed on the counter', we have no scan of an SGSU counter, so cpa 30 is borrowed from the [54.2] Truck Characteristics Chart's MEDIUM TRUCK row -- which prints THREE Capability Point Allowances for a Medium Truck Point, not one (motorizing infantry 20, motorizing guns 15, moving SUPPLIES 30). 30 is the supplies column, the largest of the three, chosen because an SGSU hauls its squadron's stores and equipment rather than troops or guns (35.0: 'SGSU's are the mechanics, trucks, equipment, etc.'). Rule 35.0 licenses the row ('the SGSU counters are considered vehicles (MEDIUM TRUCKS) and have their own Capability Point Allowance printed on the counter'); it does not license the column, which is ours. Nothing moves an SGSU yet, so the proxy is inert -- it goes live the moment 35.13/35.25 arrival-and-transfer orders land, and the counter scan settles it.
_motorcycle_comment: GE 'motorcycle_infantry' was added in the [8.45] review repair (2026-07-26) and every cell of it was READ OFF THE SCAN, not derived: [4.45c] GERMAN ORGANIZATION AT ARRIVAL CHART (PDF p.162) prints its own key -- 'Kradschutzen = Motorcycle infantry' -- and lists the 15th Kradschutzen Bn (counter 15/200, 200th Schutzen Regt, 15th Panzer Division) at PDF p.163 under ID Code 'g'; the [4.46c] GERMAN UNIT CHARACTERISTICS CHART at PDF p.137 gives ID Code 'g' as 'Infantry Bn-Eq', CPA 25, Close Assault Off/Def 3/2, Maximum TOE 7, with no anti-armor, no armor protection and NO '+' (it is not one of the historically-fully-motorized types). Those are the numbers here. A census of every ID Code on the German OA sheets (PDF p.161-175) finds 'g' used by EXACTLY ONE German counter, the 15th Kradschutzen Bn -- so 'g' IS the motorcycle-battalion row of the German chart, and its high CPA of 25 (against 10 for a lorried 'j' Schutzen battalion) is the book pricing the motorcycle's speed. The ONE thing not printed in that row is the mobility class, and it is not invented either: the rulebook names 'motorcycle infantry' as a distinct terrain/logistics class in three places, all of which now bind this counter -- [8.44] exempts it from the Salt Marsh vehicle bar, [8.45] forbids it Desert hexes entirely, and [49.12] 'Fuel users ... do not include motorcycles'. FLAGGED, NOT FIXED (a different slice, and it needs its own scan pass): the 'infantry' role above ALSO claims type 'g', but its five live German consumers are the Ramcke Brigade parachute battalions (Burchardt/Schweiger/Kroh/Heydte/Hubner), which the book gives ID Code 'h' (CPA 10, CA 3/5, may assign one paradropable artillery TOE Strength Point). FLAGGED GAP: the book fields seven Italian Bersaglieri Mitrg (motorcycle) battalions and companies on the Italian OA sheets ('Mitrg = Motorcycle'); none of them exists in this engine's Italian OOB yet, so no Italian counter can be typed here without inventing one.
_hq_dash_comment: [4.46] THE HEADQUARTERS ROW PRINTS A DASH IN CLOSE ASSAULT, AND THE DASH IS NOT A ONE. CORRECTED 2026-08-02: GE.hq, CW.hq and CW.hq_engineer carried "dca": 1 while citing chart row 'a'. That 1 is on no chart. All three [4.46] Unit Characteristics Charts were re-rendered at 300 dpi and read cell by cell for this correction. GERMAN [4.46c], PDF p.137, row a: 'Headquarters | a | 60' and then a DASH in every one of the seven rating columns -- Anti-Air, Barrage, Anti-Armor, Vulnerability, Armor Prtctn, Close Assault Off/Def, Maximum TOE. Row 'b*' is the same shape at CPA 30. COMMONWEALTH [4.46a], PDF p.133, row a: 'Headquarters | a | 30', dashes in the same seven columns. (CW row b, CPA '30*', dashes the ratings too but carries a continuation line -- 'may assign one tank TOE Strength Point' -- and a Maximum TOE of '(1)'; German row c does the same. Row 'a' carries no continuation on either chart.) THE DASH IN MAXIMUM TOE IS WHAT MAKES ROW 'a' UNAMBIGUOUS rather than a TOE placeholder: nothing can ever be assigned to it, so no rating can come into existence. The charts' own key, read off the same p.137 render, defines the mark: '- = Not applicable (e.g., an infantry unit has no Vulnerability and may therefore not be harmed by Anti-Armor fire).' No [4.46] HQ row prints a bare 1 anywhere. THE BOOK DRAWS THE DISTINCTION ITSELF on folio 6, in the target-class list: 'Infantry-class: All Infantry-Type, Engineers, Headquarters possessing a defensive Close Assault Rating but not possessing an Armor Protection Rating, SGSU, and Recce-Type that do not possess an Armor Protection Rating' -- there are HQs that possess one (the parenthesized rows, e.g. German 'e*' 0/(1), Italian 'b' 0/(1)) and HQs that do not, and row 'a' is the second kind. WHAT THE DASH DOES IN THE DEFENDER LIST -- it does NOT bar the counter from Close Assault. [15.11], PDF p.22: 'All units which possess a Close Assault Rating may use their ratings to aid in either Offensive Assault or Defense Against Assault. (Units without Ratings may also participate, even though they add nothing to the point total; see Case 15.17.)' It defends at ZERO; 15.11's own cross-reference supplies the rest -- [15.17], same page, verbatim and NOT truncated at the comma, because the qualifier is the point: 'Such units do not include their TOE Strength for determining losses when they occupy a hex with combat units unless the "losing" Player so wishes. In such a case, units with parenthesized ratings may be used to absorb losses but may not absorb more than 25% of such losses.' So it is in the stack, it retreats with it, and it neither raises the differential nor sheds a step to pay for it unless its owner elects to spend it -- an ELECTION this engine does not model and does not fake (_absorb_losses simply skips a 0-rated counter), which is the narrower of the two readings and is flagged here as the one place [15.17] is not fully built. When its stack is gone the book collects it where it stands -- [3.36], PDF p.6: 'An HQ unit that has no combat values, either with or without parentheses, is captured instantly if it is in a hex without any combat units and an Enemy combat unit places the HQ in its Zone of Control.' NO ENGINE CODE CHANGED FOR ANY OF THAT: every consequence is a rule game/engine.py already encodes, reading a rating that is finally the chart's -- _def_raw and raw_defense go to 0 (15.11), the defender_loss_raw pool and _absorb_losses drop it (15.17), _has_no_strength becomes True so the already-built [10.29] _capture_noncombat finally reaches 3.36's population (that slice's own docstring, tests/baselines.py and tests/test_noncombat_capture.py each recorded this 1 as the reason that population was EMPTY and that 'THE TWO CHANGES ARE COUPLED'), and supply.ammo_capacity goes to 0 because [50.0]'s basic load samples the combat functions a counter has and this one has none. Pinned in tests/test_hq_close_assault.py. THE ITALIAN ROWS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED -- see the IT block's _hq_dash_comment.

GE._engineer_comment: [24.3]/[24.31] Phase 8.1a's own OWN GAP, now closed: the German 'Pioneer' (= Engineer, [4.45c]'s own glossary) Battalions/Companies -- the ONLY German engineer counters the OA chart carries; the [4.46c] Unit Characteristics Chart's 'Engineer Bn/Coy-Eq' row, ID 'gg' (scan p.137): CPA 25, Close Assault Off/Def 0/(1) (the parenthesized value 23.11 gates on standing with a Friendly combat unit), Maximum TOE (1). is_combat false / oca,dca 0 / sp 0 mirror rule 23.11 ('no real combat value... not combat units in any way, shape, or form') exactly as the CW rr_engineer/road_engineer rows already do. FOOT is the chart's own answer, not a guess: the German chart prints the '+' motorization mark ('m' 10+, 'n'/'p'/'q' 8+, scan p.137) and 'gg' prints a bare 25. GERMANY HAS NO HQ-ENGINEERING COUNTER AT ALL -- every HQ row on the German OA chart ([4.45c], all 11 sheets, scan-read in full) prints plain 'HQ', never the 'HQ^E' superscript the Commonwealth and Italian charts use; this is the book's own answer, not a gap, and matches 24.31's prose scoping the HQ-lay-a-minefield capability to 'Commonwealth HQ Engineers' alone.

CW._4_46a_rows_comment: [4.46a] COMMONWEALTH UNIT CHARACTERISTICS CHART, scan PDF p.133 (codes 'a' thru 'bb') and p.134 ('cc' thru 'uu'), rendered at 300 dpi and read cell by cell. EIGHTEEN ROWS WERE ADDED 2026-08-04 by the [4.44B] order-of-battle pass (scratchpad/data-debt/cw-counters.md): hq_b/c/d/e/f, infantry_k/m/n/t/v/w, artillery_y, antitank_bb/cc/dd, light_aa_ff and recon_ll/ss. Every one is a row the chart PRINTS, needed because the 90 Commonwealth counters that pass seeded use 24 distinct ID Codes and only nine of them had a row here. NAMING: each new key is the chart's own 'Unit Type' cell plus its ID Code, because the chart is keyed by ID Code and two rows of one Unit Type differ only in that letter -- 'l' and 'n' are both Infantry Bn-Eq at CPA 10+ and differ only in Close Assault (2/2 against 1/2). WHAT IS TRANSCRIBED AND WHAT IS CONVENTION: CPA, Close Assault Off/Def, Anti-Armor, Vulnerability, Armor Protection and Maximum TOE are the chart's cells verbatim, INCLUDING ITS DASHES -- see _dash_divergence_comment for the one place that makes a new row disagree with an old one. Mobility is NOT a chart column; it follows the chart's own '+' key ('the unit was historically supplied with enough trucks to entirely motorize its components... only commonwealth battalion and company-equivalent units may be motorized'), so a '10+' row is MOTORIZED and a bare '10' row is FOOT -- the convention the pre-existing motor_infantry ('l') / infantry ('p') pair already set. is_combat false + sp 0 on the five new Headquarters rows mirrors row 'a' exactly (see _hq_dash_comment); rows 'e' and 'f' carry a printed Close Assault of 0/1 and so DEFEND at 1, but they are Headquarters counters and are not promoted to combat units here -- that would be a new ruling, and it is FLAGGED rather than taken. TWO MAXIMUM-TOE CELLS WERE ADDED TO PRE-EXISTING ROWS and nothing else on them was touched: 'g' prints Maximum TOE '10 dagger' and 'ee' prints 6, where both rows carried only their `steps` (8 and 4) and max_toe silently defaulted to it. The charted counters this pass seeds print '10 x Mark VI Lights' and '6 x Light AA' in their TOE column, so without the cell they would have been seeded OVERSTRENGTH against a ceiling the chart does not set. The pre-existing counters keep their seeded strength and simply gain the rebuild headroom [19.61] says they have. *** SAY THE REACH PLAINLY, BECAUSE 'two cells' UNDERSTATES IT (widened 2026-08-04 after the slice's own gate flagged the wording as narrow): these two cells are role defaults, so they raise the [19.61]/[19.68] rebuild ceiling and the [9.26] shell denominator for EVERY Commonwealth tank and Light-AA counter in the campaign -- all 31 tank counters and every 'ee' regiment, not only the 90 this pass added. That is the correct consequence of transcribing the row rather than a side effect to be contained: the chart sets Maximum TOE per ID Code, so every counter reading row 'g' has a ceiling of 10 and every counter reading 'ee' has 6. It is recorded here because a reader who sees 'two Maximum-TOE cells' should not have to discover the blast radius from a diff. Both benchmark signatures are byte-identical across the change (neither seeds Commonwealth reinforcements), so the widened ceiling is measured, not assumed.
CW._dash_divergence_comment: [4.46a] PRINTS A DASH IN ANTI-ARMOR ON EVERY RECONNAISSANCE ROW, AND THE PRE-EXISTING `recon` ROW DOES NOT TRANSCRIBE IT. p.134 row 'pp' reads: CPA 45 | Anti-Air - | Barrage - | Anti-Armor - | Vulnerability - | Armor Prtctn 2 | Close Assault 2/3 | Maximum TOE 6. The `recon` row below carries BOTH armor_protection 2 AND anti_armor 2 -- one value, copied into two fields, which is the signature of a column slip at transcription time. FLAGGED, PRE-EXISTING, NOT FIXED HERE: correcting it changes every already-seeded Commonwealth armoured-car regiment's anti-armor fire, which is a measured change and not this pass's. The two rows added here (recon_ll, recon_ss) transcribe the dash, so they read anti_armor 0 while their older sibling reads 2. THE INCONSISTENCY IS DELIBERATE AND IS THE DEBT MADE VISIBLE; do not 'harmonise' it by copying the 2 across -- harmonise it by deleting the 2, in a slice that measures the result. The same shape of proxy is already flagged on the gun rows for a DIFFERENT and legitimate reason: the chart prints dashes on the artillery / anti-tank / anti-air counter rows because those ratings come from the WEAPON SYSTEM assigned to the counter ([11.3] Rating x TOE / 10), so `artillery`/`antitank`/`aa` carry a representative weapon's ratings as the role default and an OOB record's `model` overrides them. artillery_y, antitank_bb/cc/dd and light_aa_ff follow that same established convention and differ from their siblings only in the chart cell that actually differs, Maximum TOE.

hq_b._chart: [4.46a] p.133 'Headquarters | b | 30* | - - - - - | (1)' with the continuation line 'may assign one tank TOE Strength Point'. The * is the chart's own key: 'The unit retains this Capability Point Allowance regardless of the CPA of the TOE Strength Points assigned.' THE TANK POINT IS NOT MODELLED ON THE COUNTER: the four counters that use this row (7th/10th Armored Div HQ, 4th Armored Bde HQ, 1st/2nd Armored Bde HQ, 8th/9th Armored Bde HQ) each print one tank in their TOE column, and assigning a weapon system's own ratings to a Headquarters is the [19.x] TOE-assignment machinery this engine has only for [19.8] ad hoc anti-tank. The row's rating columns are all dashes, so nothing is invented by leaving it; what is lost is one tank TOE Strength Point of substance. FLAGGED in the record's own _comment.

hq_c._chart: [4.46a] p.133 'Headquarters | c | 30 | - - - - - | 3' with 'may assign up to three artillery TOE Strength Points'. Same flag as hq_b: the 16th and 23rd Infantry Brigade HQs print 3 x 3.7" Howitzer / 3 x 25-pounder, and the artillery's Barrage Rating is not carried onto the HQ counter.

hq_d._chart: [4.46a] p.133 'Headquarters | d | 20* | - - - - - | (1)' with 'may assign one tank TOE Strength Point'. Identical in shape to 'b' at the lower CPA.

hq_e._chart: [4.46a] p.133 'Headquarters | e | 20 | - | - | 1 | 1 | - | 0/1 | 1'. The FIRST Headquarters rows in this file to carry a rating: Anti-Armor 1, Vulnerability 1 and an unparenthesized defensive Close Assault of 1. Folio 6's target-class list draws the distinction itself -- 'Headquarters possessing a defensive Close Assault Rating but not possessing an Armor Protection Rating' are Infantry-class targets -- so this row IS in the defender list where row 'a' defends at zero. is_combat stays false, matching row 'a': promoting a Headquarters to a ZOC-exerting, city-banking combat unit is a ruling this transcription does not get to make. FLAGGED.

hq_f._chart: [4.46a] p.133 'Headquarters | f | 20 | - | - | 2 | 1 | - | 0/1 | 1'. Same shape as 'e' at Anti-Armor 2. Used by the Australian infantry brigade HQs (16 Aus, 18 Aus, 20 Aus, 24 Aus, 26 Aus).

infantry_k._chart: [4.46a] p.133 'Infantry Bn-Eq | k | 10 | - - - - - | 2/2 | 7'. The ONLY 'k' counter on the whole Commonwealth chart is the 28th Maori Infantry Battalion (p.129, U@2, arrives 1/35), and 7 is the largest infantry Maximum TOE the chart grants anyone.

infantry_m._chart: [4.46a] p.133 'Infantry Bn-Eq | m | 10 | - - - - - | 2/2 | 6'. The unmarked twin of 'l': same Close Assault, same Maximum TOE, and NO '+' in the CPA cell, so it is not one of the historically-motorized types. The workhorse row of the British county battalions (the 44th, 50th and 51st Divisions) and of the 4th New Zealand Brigade.

infantry_n._chart: [4.46a] p.133 'Infantry Bn-Eq | n | 10+ | - - - - - | 1/2 | 6'. The '+' twin of 'p'. The 7th Armoured Division's two motor battalions (1 KRRC and 2 RflBde, p.117) and the 161st Indian Motor Brigade's two (p.128) print it.

infantry_t._chart: [4.46a] p.133 'Infantry Bn-Eq | t | 10 | - - - - - | 1/1 | 3'. Seeded by ONE counter, the Royal Yugoslav Guards (p.122, arrives 1/70) -- the counter whose ID Code the transcription had read as 'f' (a Headquarters row) until it was re-rendered at 600 dpi and cropped beside the 1st and 14th Sherwood Forresters' plain-vertical 'l'. p.134 note 2 reaches this row: 'Beginning with the 1/75 Game-Turn, infantry battalions with ID Codes of "k" thru "t" inclusive may be augmented by anti-tank TOE Strength Points (see Case 19.9)' -- unbuilt for the Commonwealth.

infantry_v._chart: [4.46a] p.133 'Infantry Company-Eq | v | 10+ | - - - - - | 1/1 | 1'. The chart's only 'v' counter is the 1st Company, French Motor Marines (p.132, arrives 3/65) -- one Strength Point, and the smallest combat counter the Commonwealth fields.

infantry_w._chart: [4.46a] p.133 'Infantry Company-Eq | w | 8 | - - - - - | 4/6 | 2'. The company-equivalent of the 'u' machinegun battalion row, at two Strength Points instead of three; the Kopanski MG Company (p.132, U@1) is its counter.

recon_ll._chart: [4.46a] p.134 'Reconnaissance Battalion-Eq | ll | 45 | - | - | - | - | 1 | 2/3 | 8'. The most-used reconnaissance row on the Commonwealth chart: the 11th Hussars, 44th and 50th and 51st Recce Regiments, the 6th/7th/9th Australian Divisional Cavalry, the 2nd New Zealand Cavalry, the Central India Horse, the 12th Lancers and the 13th DCO Lancers. It differs from 'pp' in Armor Protection (1 against 2) and Maximum TOE (8 against 6) and in NOTHING else -- see _dash_divergence_comment for the anti_armor the older row carries and the chart does not print. p.134 note 1: 'Beginning with the 1/39 Game-Turn, certain Reconnaissance units may be upgraded (see Case 20.5)' -- unbuilt.

recon_ss._chart: [4.46a] p.134 'Reconnaissance Battalion-Eq | ss | 45 | - | - | - | - | 1 | 1/2 | 4'. The weakest recce row the chart prints; the 1st Polish Cavalry Regiment (p.132) is its counter.

artillery_y._chart: [4.46a] p.133 'Artillery Battalion-Eq | y | 20 | - - - - - | 4' with 'may assign up to four artillery TOE Strength Points'. Identical to 'x' but for the four-point ceiling. Barrage and Vulnerability follow the same weapon-derived convention 'x' does (see _dash_divergence_comment) and are overridden per record by `model` -- the 1st Polish Artillery Regiment prints 4 x 18-pounder and the 1st Regt d'artillerie 4 x French 149mm.

antitank_bb._chart: [4.46a] p.133 'Anti-tank Battalion-Eq | bb | 15 | - - - - - | 6' with 'may assign up to four anti-tank TOE Strength Points and two Light Anti-Aircraft TOE Strength Points'. The MIXED row, and the chart's only counter for it is the 102(NH) Light Anti-Aircraft/Anti-Tank Regt (p.117, 2 x 2-pounders + 2 x Light AA, arrives 1/15). The engine carries one weapon system per counter, so the record names the anti-tank half and its two Light AA points ride the same four-point arrival TOE -- FLAGGED in the record.

antitank_cc._chart: [4.46a] p.134 'Anti-tank Company-Eq | cc | 15 | - - - - - | 4' with 'may assign up to four anti-tank TOE Strength Points'. The two Free French anti-tank companies print it: 2 NA (p.131, 4 x 2-pounder, 3/63) and 23 NA (p.132, 3 x 2-pounder, 3/75).

antitank_dd._chart: [4.46a] p.134 'Anti-tank Company-Eq | dd | 15 | - - - - - | 2' with 'may assign up to two anti-tank TOE Strength Points'. The 70th Division's three brigade anti-tank companies (p.120) and the 1st Polish Anti-tank Company (p.132) print it.

light_aa_ff._chart: [4.46a] p.134 'Light Anti-air Bn-Eq | ff | 15 | - - - - - | 4' with 'may assign up to four Light AA TOE Strength Points'. The four-point sibling of 'ee'. Its one counter is the 1st Bn de fusiliers (p.131, `1 Fslrs`, 4 x Light AA, arrives 3/63), which this OOB had seeded as an infantry battalion. Ground stats follow the 'ee' row's FLAGGED proxy (see _aa_air_comment) and the record names the `light_aa` model.

CW._engineer_comment: [23.0]/[24.61]/[23.13] The Commonwealth's construction units. The Construction Chart's footnote f names them: 'the Commonwealth Player's one South African Road Construction Battalion and two New Zealand Railroad Construction Battalions'; 24.61 names the NZRRC pair by number ('the 10th and the 13th') and makes them THE ONLY UNITS IN THE GAME THAT MAY BUILD RAILROAD. is_combat false, oca/dca 0 and sp 0 are the RULE (23.11: engineers 'have no real combat value, nor do they exert Zones of Control... not combat units in any way, shape, or form'). The `engineer` field is what they may be USED for -- 23.13: the NZRRC are 'used solely for the construction and repair of Railroads', the 1 S.A. Road Construction unit 'solely for Road work'. The road battalion is SEEDED BUT IDLE: rule 24.5 road construction is not implemented (the map's unfinished-road hexes are untranscribed), so it exists as the rulebook's counter and builds nothing yet. CPA CORRECTED 2026-07-27 (Phase 8.1b engineer-OOB pass): both rows carried a PROXY CPA of 30 (mirroring the CW hq row) because '[4.46a] ... is untranscribed' -- it no longer is. The [4.46a] Commonwealth Unit Characteristics Chart's own 'Construction (Road/RR)' row, ID 'uu' (scan p.134): CPA 25, Close Assault Off/Def 0/(1), Maximum TOE (1). The two Railroad/Road counters and the Tobruk-garrison/RECAM/etc Engineer-Bn-Eq counters share this one row -- the chart does not separate them. MOBILITY CORRECTED 2026-07-27 in the 8.1b review repair, MOTORIZED -> FOOT, from the same row and the chart's own key: '+ = The unit was historically supplied with enough trucks to entirely motorize its components. Note that only commonwealth battalion and company-equivalent units may be motorized' (scan p.134, read verbatim). The mark is printed in the CPA cell -- ID 'l' 10+, 'n' 10+, 'v' 10+ on p.133 -- and 'uu' prints a bare 25, so the chart says these battalion-equivalents are NOT motorized. The MOTORIZED they carried was a leftover of the CPA-30 proxy this pass replaced; keeping half of a row one has just cited is how a transcription starts lying. FLAGGED, PRE-EXISTING, NOT FIXED HERE: the '+' column is not transcribed ANYWHERE else in this file. Most conspicuously the CW 'hq' row (ID 'a', CPA 30, no '+') is MOTORIZED, and hq_engineer mirrors it by 23.14. HQs are not 'battalion and company-equivalent units', so the key's sentence does not even reach them -- but every other MOTORIZED row here predates the [4.46a/b/c] transcription and none has been checked against its '+' mark. That is a whole-chart pass of its own, on units that fight.
CW._hq_engineer_comment: [23.14]/[4.44B] The Commonwealth division/brigade HQs the [4.44B] OA chart marks 'HQ^E' ('Headquarters with engineering capability' -- the chart's own TYPE key, scan p.116). Same base stats as the plain 'hq' row above (the chart does not print a separate CPA/rating row for HQ^E -- 23.14: 'they are otherwise treated like any other HQ unit'); the only difference is the `engineer` flag, which unlocks 24.31 (lay a minefield -- Commonwealth-only per 24.31's own prose), 23.21/26.24 (escort discount), 23.22 (sit-still clearing), 23.23 (help build), 23.24 (assault shift). NOT every CW division HQ carries it -- the chart marks some and not others with no visible pattern (7th Armoured yes, 1st/2nd/8th/10th Armoured no; 70th/44th/50th/51st Infantry yes, 9th Australian no) -- so this role is applied per OA-chart-verified record, never as a blanket default. MOBILITY: this row copies the plain 'hq' row cell for cell ON PURPOSE -- 23.14 says an HQ^E is 'otherwise treated like any other HQ unit', so any difference between the two rows other than the `engineer` flag would BE the bug. If the CW hq row's MOTORIZED is ever corrected against the [4.46a] '+' key (see _engineer_comment above), this row moves with it. 23.11 DOES NOT BIND THIS ROW: game.minefields.is_engineer_counter exempts HQ_ENGINEER on that same 23.14 sentence, so an HQ^E may enter an enemy-controlled hex exactly as a plain HQ may. SEEDED 2026-07-27 (Phase 8.1c division-HQ pass, hexes corrected in its review repair). This paragraph used to read "FLAGGED, NOT SEEDED -- four Commonwealth HQ^E the [4.44B] chart prints have NO counter in this repo to carry the flag", and it also miscounted: there are FIVE, not four. All five now exist. 7th Armored Div HQ^E (scan p.117, counter "7", ID "b", D) and 4th Indian Div HQ^E (p.126, "4 In", "a", D) are at-start records in data/oob_campaign_extra.json, at the hexes [60.41] Commonwealth Initial Deployment prints for them -- D3612 and D3615, each with its own units marked "Det" and standing elsewhere, which is why neither HQ sits with its brigade. 6th Australian Div HQ^E (p.124, "6 Aus", "a", D) and 2nd New Zealand Div HQ^E (p.129, "2 NZ", "a", D) are likewise at-start, at [60.41] own Helwan (E1430, "In Training") and Alexandria (E3613); the 8.1c pass had made those two GT7/GT2 reinforcements, which the chart Arrives column ("D") and [60.41] both contradict. 44th Infantry Div HQ^E (p.118, "44", "a", 2/90) is a reinforcement at its charted 2/90. The pre-existing extraction gap this paragraph used to describe is real and unchanged in kind -- the raw VASSAL campaign extraction carries ZERO HQ counters of ANY kind for EITHER side -- but the answer to it is the OA charts, which print every one of these counters, not silence. The OCR in docs/rules/90-charts misses the 2nd NZ and 2nd Free French HQ^E entirely, which is why these were read off the scan.

IT._comment: Italian role stats -- representative (weaker CA, older kit than German); tank/gun MODELS (M13/M14 etc.) come from the [4.48] chart via each unit's model. Flagged for [4.46] Italian Unit Characteristics Chart verification.
IT._hq_dash_comment: [4.46b] WHY THE ITALIAN HQ ROWS KEEP THEIR 1 WHILE GE.hq / CW.hq / CW.hq_engineer WENT TO 0 (2026-08-02). It is NOT an oversight and it must not be 'finished' by a later sweep; tests/test_hq_close_assault.py pins it. THE ITALIAN CHART WAS RE-RENDERED at 300 dpi for this pass (PDF p.136, printed sideways) and read cell by cell. Its Headquarters block does NOT match the German/Commonwealth one: row 'a*' prints CPA 45 -- with dashes across the ratings and a continuation line, 'may assign one reconnaisance TOE Strenth Point' (the book's own two typos), Maximum TOE '(1)' -- while row 'b' prints CPA 30 with dashes in Anti-Air, Barrage, Anti-Armor, Vulnerability and Armor Prtctn but Close Assault Off/Def '0/(1)' and Maximum TOE '(1)'; row 'c' prints CPA '30*', Anti-Armor '(1)', Armor Prtctn '(1)', Close Assault '(3)/(2)', Maximum TOE '(1)'. THE ENGINE WRITES CPA 30, WHICH IS ROW b, NOT THE ROW 'a' THE type CELL CLAIMS -- and row b prints a RATING, not a dash. So the two candidate readings disagree: row 'a' would say dash, row b (the CPA the engine actually uses) says 0/(1). Writing a 0 here would be transcribing a row this repo has not identified, i.e. inventing; keeping the 1 is the pre-existing unverified approximation of row b's '(1)', which this engine has no parenthesized-rating mechanic to express exactly. Both are flagged, neither is silent. THE UNDERLYING DEBT IS ALREADY ON RECORD TWICE in this block: the _comment above flags the whole IT block for '[4.46] Italian Unit Characteristics Chart verification', and _hq_engineer_comment concedes that the nine Italian HQ^E counters carry three different ID Codes (b, d and f) and that 'no Italian HQ ID Code is transcribed from [4.46b] yet'. That transcription is the slice that settles this cell; until it lands, the consequence is a KNOWN AND FLAGGED ASYMMETRY -- an Italian bare HQ is not in [3.36]/[10.29]'s capture population while a German or Commonwealth one now is, because on the numbers this repo has transcribed the Italian counter still has 'strength of a type' and the German/Commonwealth ones provably do not.
IT._engineer_comment: [24.3]/[24.31] The Italian 'Genio' (Engineer) Battalions -- fifteen of them on the [4.44b] OA chart, one per infantry/CCNN division plus RECAM's Guastatori and the Tobruk/Benghazi garrison ones, all ID 'bbb' EXCEPT the Benghazi Garrison's VIII/II Engineer Bn, which prints 'bb' (an Infantry Bn-Eq row, CPA 8, Close Assault 5/7) -- almost certainly a book misprint for 'bbb' (23.11 makes an Engineer counter structurally incapable of carrying an infantry combat rating; no other Engineer Bn on the whole chart uses any code but 'bbb'). NOTHING IS TRANSCRIBED FOR IT YET: the Benghazi Garrison's VIII/II counter is not seeded from this row at all -- it is one of the four already-seeded '(ENG)'-tagged Italian records that still build as combat infantry (see game.oob.classify's '(ENG)' branch), so this paragraph is the misprint FLAG, not an applied override. The [4.46b] Italian Unit Characteristics Chart's own 'Engineer Bat-Eq' row, ID 'bbb' (scan p.136): CPA 25, Close Assault Off/Def 0/(1), Maximum TOE (1) -- same shape as the German 'gg' row. is_combat false / oca,dca 0 / sp 0 mirror rule 23.11. FOOT is the chart's own answer, not a guess: the Italian chart prints the same '+' motorization mark the Commonwealth one does (ID 'hh' reads '8+', scan p.136) and 'bbb' prints a bare 25. Italy ALSO carries HQ-Engineering, and as of 2026-07-27 (the 8.1c review repair) it is SEEDED, not flagged: see the IT _hq_engineer_comment below.
IT._hq_engineer_comment: [23.14]/[4.45b] THE ITALIAN HQ^E ROW. SEEDED 2026-07-27 in the 8.1c review repair; before that the 8.1c pass seeded all nine of these counters and then gave every one of them the plain `hq` role, which silently dropped the engineering capability the chart hands the Axis -- each record comment said "HQ^E" and then set the non-E role. The [4.44b] TYPE key prints the distinction itself (scan p.147, read verbatim off a 200dpi render for this repair): "TYPE: HQ^E = Headquarters with engineering capability; HQ = Headquarters without engineering capability." NINE Italian rows carry the superscript, and they are the nine this role is applied to, each read on its own sheet: Ariete (132nd) Div HQ^E (p.147), Littorio (133rd) Div HQ^E / 1st Libyan Infantry HQ^E / 2nd Libyan Infantry HQ^E (p.148), 136th Giovani Fascisti Div HQ^E and 185th Folgore Div HQ^E (p.154), 31st and 32nd Gaf S di C HQ^E (p.155, the Tobruk Garrison sheet), 30th Gaf S di C HQ^E (p.156, Bardia). CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE COUNTER ART: a census of the Eng layer across all 1,642 counter SVGs in the CNAv2.1.0 VASSAL module finds exactly 22 counters drawn with the E, and its nine Italian ones are these nine, counter for counter (IT Ariete/Littorio/185 Folg/136 GGFF/1 Libyan/2 Libyan - none, IT 30 GaF - Bardia, IT 31 Gaf/32 Gaf - Tobruk). RECAM HQ is NOT one of them -- the chart prints it a plain HQ (p.154) and the art draws no E -- so it keeps the `hq` role; the distinction is per row, not per nation. TWO DISAGREEMENTS BETWEEN THE ART AND THE BOOK, both resolved for the BOOK (port rule 2, the same way the Pz III E was): the art also puts an E on "IT 1 Libyan - 1 Libyan" and "IT 2 Libyan - 1 Libyan", the two Libyan REGIMENT HQs, which p.148 prints as plain "1st/2nd Libyan Regt HQ" (ID h) -- neither is seeded in this OOB in any case; and the art omits the E from "AU 6 Aus - none", "NZ 2 NZ - none" and the 5th Indian division HQ, which p.124/p.129/p.126 print HQ^E. STATS: this row copies the IT `hq` row cell for cell and adds only the `engineer` flag, on 23.14 ("they are otherwise treated like any other HQ unit") -- exactly the rule the CW hq_engineer row cites for the same copy. WHAT IT UNLOCKS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT: [24.42] "AnyE" fortification row is EITHER SIDE, so an Italian HQ^E may raise a Level of fortification (game.construction.builds_engineering) and confers 23.21/26.24 escort and 23.22 clearing; [24.31]/[24.17] minefield rows read "EBn, ECoy or CHQ-E" = ALLIED headquarters only, so it may NOT sow mines (game.construction.lays_minefield already keeps that asymmetry). FLAGGED, PRE-EXISTING: the chart gives these nine HQs three different ID Codes (b, d and f) and the IT `hq` row type cell says "a"; no Italian HQ ID Code is transcribed from [4.46b] yet, which is the same debt the IT block opening _comment already carries for every role in it. This row inherits that debt rather than inventing a second answer.

_models_comment: Per-model combat ratings from the Tank & Gun Characteristics Charts (4.47/4.48/4.49), extracted this session. A unit may name a 'model' to override its role's combat ratings (only the fields present are overridden; steps/cpa/mobility stay from the role). Tank models set oca/dca/anti_armor/armor_protection/is_tank; gun models set anti_armor/vulnerability; artillery set barrage/vulnerability (25pdr also anti_armor).
_bar_comment: 'bar' = Breakdown Adjustment Rating (rule 21.3), the per-model column shift applied on the [21.38] Breakdown Table BEFORE rolling. Signed integer convention: +N = N columns to the RIGHT (more breakdown, less reliable), -N = N LEFT, 0 = none. Sources: German [4.49], Italian [4.48], and Commonwealth [4.47] Tank & Gun Characteristics Charts (see data/breakdown_rates.json 'bar_by_model' for the full recovered chart, incl. the CW column that had to be read off the PDF scan and the trucks' 54.2 -2). German tanks: all 0 except the early Pz III E (BAR 3, Eve-confirmed on scan p.140) (chart note *: temporarily +1 / 1R until Game-Turn 1/31 -- a turn-gate to honor in the reader, not a flat value). Gun/AT/artillery models carry NO 'bar': towed guns with inherent transport never break down (21.11), a '-' on the chart. DATA ONLY -- no engine code reads 'bar' yet.
_phase3_2_comment: Phase 3.2 (2026-07-17): the 56 weapon-system models that were MISSING from the Tank & Gun charts, transcribed from [4.47] Commonwealth (scan PDF p.138), [4.48] Italian (p.139) and [4.49] German (p.140) via scratchpad/port/phase3-oob-gap.json, each cell cross-checked against its verbatim _chart row there. Engine-read fields only (oca/dca/barrage/anti_armor/armor_protection/vulnerability/is_tank/bar); the charts' AA anti-air rating, CPA and Fuel Rate are not per-model engine inputs (CPA comes from the role, fuel from logistics_rates.json) and stay in the gap doc. Italian and German guns are it_/de_-prefixed so the two nations' identically-named captured pieces (149mm Vichy French) do not collide. These models are inert until an OOB record names one via 'model' (none does yet), so adding them changes no built state. Pz III E is NOW SEEDED (2026-07-18): its [4.49] row was misprinted in the 1979 book and the CNAv2.1.0 VASSAL remaster (images/German Tank and Gun Characteristics Chart.png) read it Armor Prtctn 3 / BAR 0, but Eve visually confirmed Armor-Protection 4 / BAR 3 against scan p.140 -- the prep best-inference reading -- resolving the VASSAL-remaster discrepancy. Like the other Phase-3.2 models it is inert (no OOB record names it yet, so no built state changes) and awaits an OOB reference (likely 5 Le Div ~GT21-26).

aus_pioneer._engineer: [4.44B] OA chart note b, 9TH AUSTRALIAN DIVISION sheet (scan p.125 -- the counter is printed there as '2/1 Pioneer Bn', counter abbreviation '2/1 AusP', ID Code 'q', Arrives 3/29; the 18th Australian Brigade sheet on the same page is a different roster and an earlier note said so in error): 'Pioneer Battalions in the Australian army were engineer battalions with full-fledged infantry capabilities. This unit possesses all normal engineer battalion capabilities plus those of its q ID Code.' The ONE Commonwealth general Engineer Battalion (EBn) this OOB seeds -- every other CW engineer capability is RAIL/ROAD (their one named job, 23.13) or HQ-Engineering (game.minefields.GENERAL_ENGINEER via lays_minefield). Model-over-role, the same precedence the Scorpion uses: role stays 'infantry' (its combat stats are ordinary infantry, per the note), only the engineer flag is added. BECAUSE the note gives it 'full-fledged infantry capabilities', 23.11's restrictions do NOT reach it: game.minefields.is_engineer_counter reads 23.11 against its own stated premise ('not combat units in any way, shape, or form'), which this counter -- is_combat true, exerting a ZOC, ID 'q' at CPA 10 and Close Assault 1/1 -- does not meet. It keeps every engineer CAPABILITY (24.31 laying, 26.13 clearing, 26.24 escorting) and loses only the engineer's movement ban.
